blocks.heading: Reading climate graphs
blocks.text: A climate graph usually combines monthly precipitation totals with monthly mean temperatures, using separately labelled axes. Read the months and hemisphere context before identifying the seasons. Rainfall is commonly shown with bars and temperature with a line, but the legend controls the interpretation. Add the twelve complete monthly rainfall values for annual rainfall. For annual temperature range, subtract the lowest monthly mean from the highest. Do not average rainfall bars when the task asks for the annual total or use the hottest day’s temperature in place of the monthly mean.

In supplied series A, monthly rainfall is 180,160,190,180,170,160,140,130,150,170,180,190 mm. The annual total is 2,000 mm. Monthly mean temperature varies from 26 to 27°C, giving a 1°C annual range. The high year-round rainfall and small temperature range support an equatorial-rainforest interpretation. They do not prove a particular wind direction or that a shower occurred every day. A graph summarises observations at its stated scale and period, not every event within each bar.

Series B has rainfall 100,90,80,40,10,0,0,0,5,25,60,90 mm and monthly means ranging from 18 to 27°C. Its total is 500 mm and temperature range 9°C. The concentration of rain towards the start and end of the calendar year is consistent with a Southern Hemisphere summer-wet example. Series C totals 20 mm and has a 13°C temperature range, supporting an inland tropical-desert model. Always retain the stated synthetic status of these examples rather than attributing their invented numbers to the Amazon, East Africa or Namibia.

![Climate graphs for invented series A, B and C](../../assets/images/ITEM-6137-1.7-017-INTERP-answer.png)

blocks.text: When estimating the wettest or driest period, identify the exact months and values from the resource. An annual total can conceal a long dry interval, so two places with equal annual rain may offer different growing conditions. The timing matters alongside the amount.
